name: Rays Rising from the Root, Dissolving above the Crown

dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24, sequential, one verse per dhāraṇā for 1–16)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: āmūlāt kiraṇābhāsāṃ sūkṣmāt sūkṣmatarātmikām | cintayet tāṃ dviṣaṭkānte śāmyantīṃ bhairavodayaḥ ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, checked against Singh, Wallis's concordance and Pradīpaka
sanskrit_variants: GRETIL e-text reads sūkṣmatarātmikam and śyāmyantīm; Wallis, Pradīpaka and Singh read sūkṣmatarātmikām and śāmyantīm ('coming to rest'). The GRETIL forms look like input errors; the common reading is used here.
dharana.rendering: Contemplate her, the power, shining like rays of light from the root, becoming subtler than the subtlest, until she comes to rest in the 'end of twelve' (dviṣaṭkānta, the dvādaśānta above the crown); then Bhairava arises.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer; not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh glosses 'the root' as the mūlādhāra cakra and dviṣaṭkānta as dvādaśānta. The Mystery Within glosses the end point as the sahasrāra cakra. The verse itself says only 'from the root' and 'at the end of twelve'.
dharana.technique_name: Rays Rising from the Root, Dissolving above the Crown

checked_against: GRETIL, Pradīpaka and Wallis: verse text matches the technique
verification.notes: Door index = Singh dharana number, verified directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against at least one independent edition. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

numbering_variants.wallis_yukti: Y2 (Wallis groups verses 24–27 as one technique)
numbering_variants.popular_lists: Old notes say some popular lists number a different technique as 5; that claim could not be traced to a named edition and is unverified.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 28 does not prescribe a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: root (Singh: mūlādhāra, base of the spine)
end of twelve (dvādaśānta), above the crown
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The dharana's map is a vertical line of light rising from the root of the body to a point above the crown, growing finer until it dissolves.
geometry.svg_hint: a fine vertical line from the base of the spine through the crown to a point above the head, fading as it rises
geometry.honesty: Redefined in 2026-10: geometry now records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Base rise
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: something dense at the base thins upward into finer and finer light until it dissolves. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: ordinary breath, low and easy; the visualisation does not ride the breath
breath.cue: Ordinary breath, about four in and four out if counting helps. No forced hold. Do not pump or push the breath to make the light rise.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Orient upward along the centre line, from the base toward the space above the head
orientation.gravity: Weight settled into the support at the base; the rising is imagined, not muscular
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: A fine line of light rising from the root and thinning toward the point above the crown
attention.chakra: mūlādhāra (Singh's gloss of 'the root'; the verse says only 'root')

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: Contemplate her, the power, shining like rays of light from the root, becoming subtler than the subtlest, until she comes to rest in the 'end of twelve' (dviṣaṭkānta, the dvādaśānta above the crown); then Bhairava arises.
adiyogi.method_summary: Rest attention at the base of the body, then imagine a soft radiance rising along the centre line, growing subtler and subtler until it dissolves in the space above the crown. Ordinary breath. Do not force heat, shaking, breath retention or dramatic effects.

honesty.disclosure: Door 005 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 5 (verse 28) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type stays school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's. The original honesty text is kept below in honesty.legacy, with retired posture names redacted; the verbatim text is at previous_file.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 005 is dharana 5, verse 28. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.
Reframed from the earlier posture framing on 2026-10-06; awaiting guardian re-review. The previous review covered the posture framing only.

legacy.disclosure: This [retired posture] and VBT dharana 005 are linked by the School of 112 Doorways as a teaching device (Door 005 with dharana 005). It is not a claim of ancient one-to-one canon.
legacy.notes: Supportive resonance only: [retired posture]’s grounded back knee and upright rising centerline make a base-to-rise attention map easy to feel, which echoes dharana 005’s contemplation of luminosity rising from muladhara and subtling toward dvadasanta. Pairing remains school_device by door index. Edition note: Jaideva Singh / Lakshmanjoo number dharana 5 as verse 28 (muladhara sun-ray rise). Some popular web indexes place a nose-tip bindu method at dharana 5; this door follows the Jaideva Singh numbering used for House 1.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain in the front knee, back knee, hips, or low back.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Visualisation only, with ordinary breath. If the practice brings agitation, heat, shaking or strong emotion, stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.

legacy_notes.open_seat_alternate: If kneeling is unavailable: take a [retired posture] with the back knee lifted and hands on blocks, or practice the rising-attention thread seated upright in an open seat.
legacy_notes.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Pad the back knee. Keep the front knee tracking over the ankle, not collapsing inward. Skip deep backbending versions if the low back complains.
legacy_notes.status: Posture-specific cautions, kept for traceability; they no longer apply because this door teaches no posture.

beats.title: Name the door
beats.script: This is Door 005: rays rising from the root and dissolving above the crown. Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 5, verse 28.

beats.title: Geometry
beats.script: No shape to make. Any steady seat, or lie down. The map is a fine vertical line: from the base of the body, up the centre, to a point above the head.

beats.title: Orientation
beats.script: Let the base settle heavy into the support. Eyes closed or lowered. Orient upward along the centre line.

beats.title: Breath
beats.script: Ordinary breath, about four in and four out. No forced hold. The breath does not push the light.

beats.title: Attention
beats.script: Rest at the base. Imagine soft light rising, finer and finer, toward the space above the crown.

beats.title: Reaction cue
beats.script: School image: density at the base thins into fine light. Metaphor only.

beats.title: Adiyogi thread
beats.script: Verse 28: contemplate the power shining like rays from the root, ever subtler, coming to rest above the crown; then Bhairava arises. Ordinary breath. No force, no performance.

beats.title: Exit / integrate
beats.script: Let the image go. Feel the weight of the body and the floor. Open the eyes.
